corrections.claimed_speedup: Insert & Erase 100M int, both maps using robin_hood::hash: robin_hood::unordered_flat_map 16.9s / 1717MB vs std::unordered_map 99.7s / 3986MB (5.9x faster); robin_hood::unordered_node_map 45.5s / 2293MB (2.2x faster) (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: Author's 2019 multi-map benchmark series (map_benchmark): insert/clear/reinsert/erase of 100M int pairs, random insert/erase of uint64_t and std::string, successful/unsuccessful find over 1-2000, 1-500k uint64_t and 1-1M std::string keys, and iteration; each map run with 5 hashes (robin_hood::hash, absl::Hash, FNV1a, libstdc++ std::hash, folly::hasher), median of 9 runs.
corrections.caveats: Repo archived since 2023; the author points users to unordered_dense. Results are from 2019 (g++ 8.2, libstdc++) and first-party. Other sub-pages, same robin_hood::hash, flat map vs std::unordered_map (derived): Insert & Erase uint64_t 11.8s vs 55.2s (4.7x); Find 1-500k uint64_t 14.4 vs 53.2 ns avg (3.7x); Iterating 8.87s vs 25.4s (2.9x); Find 1-1M std::string 38.0 vs 107 ns avg (2.8x). With libstdc++'s identity std::hash on integer keys the robin_hood maps time out in several benchmarks, so the win depends on its own default robin_hood::hash. Methodology is on the overview page https://martin.ankerl.com/2019/04/01/hashmap-benchmarks-01-overview/.
